package_info.why_malicious: Multiple versions of the ua-parser-js package were compromised in a supply chain attack, with malicious code injected to download and execute cryptominers and password-stealing Trojans on both Linux and Windows systems. The package, widely used as a dependency, was weaponized to infect developer and production environments upon installation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (postinstall), the code downloads a shell script from a remote server and executes it, resulting in the installation of a cryptominer or password-stealing Trojan.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes a remote script fetched over the network during package installation, which is a common technique for delivering malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not execute arbitrary remote code during installation; postinstall scripts are typically used for setup or build tasks, not for downloading and running external binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download pre-built binaries for performance reasons, but these should always use secure, verified sources and checksums.
key_indicators: Use of child_process to execute shell commands
Fetching and executing code from an untrusted remote domain
No user interaction or consent required

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (postinstall), the code downloads a Windows executable from a remote server and runs it, leading to the installation of a password-stealing Trojan.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and executes a Windows binary without user knowledge, a classic malware delivery method.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not download and execute arbitrary binaries, especially from untrusted sources, during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some build tools may download platform-specific helpers, but these are typically signed and verified.
key_indicators: Use of PowerShell to download and execute binaries
No integrity verification of downloaded files

attack_chain.action: User or CI system installs the compromised ua-parser-js package, triggering the postinstall script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code execution on the host system.

attack_chain.action: Malicious postinstall script downloads and executes a cryptominer or password-stealing Trojan, depending on the operating system.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, resource hijacking, and credential theft.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts invoking child_process to execute shell or PowerShell commands
Network requests to untrusted or unexpected domains during package installation
Execution of downloaded binaries or scripts immediately after package install
file_indicators: Presence of unexpected postinstall.js or modified lifecycle scripts in node_modules/ua-parser-js
Downloaded files in system temp directories (e.g., /tmp/malware.sh, C:\Windows\Temp\malware.exe)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the legitimate ua-parser-js project
Connections to known malware distribution domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for unexpected postinstall script execution, especially those invoking child_process to run shell or PowerShell commands. Flag any network activity from build or CI environments to untrusted domains during package installation. Inspect node_modules for unauthorized modifications to lifecycle scripts. Use endpoint protection to detect execution of downloaded binaries or scripts from temp directories.
